title: 5 ASEAN member states support regional oil stockpiling --DTI's Roque
summary: Trade Secretary Cristina Roque on Monday said that five member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have agreed to stockpile oil in the region to address supply disruptions.

blocks.text: Trade Secretary Cristina Roque on Monday said that five member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have agreed to stockpile oil in the region to address supply disruptions.

In a press conference during the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, Roque said the countries that backed the proposed regional oil stockpiling include the Philippines, Singapore, Indonesia, and Malaysia.
The United Arab Emirates, meanwhile, has also expressed interest to “put oil inventories in countries that have facilities to stock this oil.”
“For the oil stockpiling, there are five member states that have already agreed to this. So they will stockpile, or they will stock oil in the different ASEAN countries,” Roque said.

“This will make it easier also in case a country needs oil, rather than buying oil from countries that are far. To lessen the cost also, the logistics cost, we can now purchase across ASEAN,” she added.
The Trade Secretary said that the Philippines, as chair of ASEAN for 2026, led the discussions on the planned regional oil stockpiling during the summit.
She noted that this was an initiative championed by President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr.

“This will enable ASEAN member-states to manage supply disruptions and reduce risks to businesses and consumers during periods of global uncertainties. By having access to regional oil stockpiles during times of need, countries can respond more effectively to supply shocks, helping stabilize energy supplies and prices,” Roque said.
“ERIA will submit now their studies on stockpiling,” she added.
In September, the Department of Energy (DOE) said the government is promoting the Philippines to be an oil storage hub for the whole of Asia.
The plan, according to DOE, is to allow other countries to build storage facilities in the country. —AOL, GMA News
